full_judgment:
2. The suit was filed by the plaintiffs for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for permanent injunction. The plaintiff’s case is that the suit land together with other lands originally belonged to one Jonab Ali Sardar who gave settlement of 27.38 acres of land in favour of his son-in-law, Abdul Hamid in the middle of Baisakh, 1355 BS at a salami of Taka 3,000.00 with yearly rent of Taka 135/12 and 6 pies. Abdul Hamid was in possession after settlement and paid rent to Janab Ali Sardar (landlord). There being default in payment of rent Janab Ali Sardar (landlord) instituted Rent Suit No. 826 of 1956 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Satkhira against the said Abdul Hamid for arrear of rent and got the decree. Duirng SA operation the suit land was recorded in the name of Abdul Hamid in the SA Khatian. Abdul Hamid died in 1971, leaving behind his wife Jahura Khatun and 2 sons Baki Billah and Moniruzzaman. Thereafter by two kabalas the suit land was transferred to the plaintiffs by the heirs of the said Abdul Hamid. The plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land on their own rights and on 23-6-82 the defendants threatened the plaintiffs to remove the earth from the suit land. Hence, the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1-5 by filing a joint written statement admitted that the suit land originally belonged to Janab Ali Sardar but asserted that he made a settlement of 27.38 acres of land in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in the first part of Baishakh, 1358 BS. These two defendants were minors at the time of settlement and as such their maternal grandfathers Jonab Ali Moral and Mohar Ali Sardar respectively did everything in taking settlement and in paying the rent and salami to landlord Janab Ali Sardar. Since settlement the defendants maternal grandfathers used to possess that suit land and looked after the same during their life time on behalf of the defendants. Thereafter the defendants themselves have been possessing the suit land and PRR khatian was prepared in their names. The SA Khatian was wrongly prepared in the name of Abdul Hamid and subsequently the same was also corrected in favour of the defendants. According to the defendants the plaintiffs kabalas are without any consideration and those did not create any title in favour of the plaintiffs. Hence the suit is liable to be dismissed.
